items.html: Governor Gavin Newsom's office announced on 09-29 that he signed AB 1556, which makes recovery housing that follows Housing First rules clearly eligible for state homelessness funding, a year after he vetoed a similar sober-housing bill. CalMatters reports the law by Assemblymember Matt Haney requires funded sober residences to have a written relapse policy and, after a relapse, to offer a move to low-barrier housing (a resident who declines can be evicted); the Assembly Appropriations Committee put the cost at about $200,000 a year for one staff position, and some housing groups opposed it as a diversion from low-barrier models. (Governor of California, CalMatters)

items.title: UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said on 09-29 that the coming ban on under-16s using high-risk social media is only a "staging post" toward an "active interventionist state" policing online spaces, ahead of her Labour conference speech.
items.html: UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said on 09-29 that the coming ban on under-16s using high-risk social media is only a "staging post" toward an "active interventionist state" policing online spaces, ahead of her Labour conference speech. The Guardian reports the ban takes effect by March, with limits on infinite scrolling and harmful-content algorithms and tighter age checks for 16- and 17-year-olds to follow, and that the government's consultation drew more than 116,000 responses, with 85% of parents saying the risk outweighed any benefit. (The Guardian)

items.title: The Children's Hospital Association, Speak Our Minds, Children's Healthcare Canada and the UK's Children's Hospital Alliance launched the Global Preventing Youth Suicide Collaborative on 09-29, to coordinate how pediatric health systems in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom identify and support young people at risk of suicide.
items.html: The Children's Hospital Association, Speak Our Minds, Children's Healthcare Canada and the UK's Children's Hospital Alliance launched the Global Preventing Youth Suicide Collaborative on 09-29, to coordinate how pediatric health systems in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom identify and support young people at risk of suicide. The Association says it grows out of a Behavioral Health Learning Collaborative of more than 40 children's hospitals whose work included more than one million youth suicide-risk screenings, and notes that more than 40% of US young people who attempted suicide had seen a provider in the previous month. (Children's Hospital Association, Chief Healthcare Executive)

items.title: A federal judge ruled on 09-23 that a class action accusing Blue Shield of California and its behavioral-health contractor Magellan of publishing a grossly inaccurate directory of mental-health clinicians can go forward, granting the motions to dismiss in part and denying the rest (reported 09-29).
items.html: A federal judge ruled on 09-23 that a class action accusing Blue Shield of California and its behavioral-health contractor Magellan of publishing a grossly inaccurate directory of mental-health clinicians can go forward, granting the motions to dismiss in part and denying the rest (reported 09-29). Judge William Orrick's order in Roiz v. Blue Shield dismissed two causes of action against Blue Shield and five against Magellan, with leave to amend within 20 days; Behavioral Health Business reports the amended complaint is due 10-13, after which discovery and class certification follow, and that Blue Shield does not comment on pending litigation. (Order, N.D. Cal., Behavioral Health Business)

items.title: Prairie St. John's Hospital, a private 132-bed psychiatric and addiction-treatment hospital in Fargo, agreed to a $5.5 million settlement, effective 07-10, of allegations that it improperly billed and double-billed North Dakota Medicaid and a state addiction voucher program, and the agreement bars the state from announcing it (reported 09-29).
items.html: Prairie St. John's Hospital, a private 132-bed psychiatric and addiction-treatment hospital in Fargo, agreed to a $5.5 million settlement, effective 07-10, of allegations that it improperly billed and double-billed North Dakota Medicaid and a state addiction voucher program, and the agreement bars the state from announcing it (reported 09-29). A column in The Forum quotes the agreement as saying the state agencies "agree not to issue a press release," while chief executive Ty Hegland says the hospital denies wrongdoing, calls it a "highly technical billing matter" over Medicaid's exclusion for institutions for mental disease, and says no deficient care was alleged. (The Forum)

items.title: A Massachusetts judge took under advisement a defence motion to find Lindsay Clancy not guilty and a double-jeopardy motion to dismiss on 09-29, three weeks after her trial for the deaths of her three children ended in an 11-1 mistrial; prosecutors have not said whether they will retry her, and the next hearing is 11-02.
items.html: A Massachusetts judge took under advisement a defence motion to find Lindsay Clancy not guilty and a double-jeopardy motion to dismiss on 09-29, three weeks after her trial for the deaths of her three children ended in an 11-1 mistrial; prosecutors have not said whether they will retry her, and the next hearing is 11-02. At the first hearing since the 09-04 mistrial, defence attorney Kevin Reddington argued prosecutors had not proved Clancy killed the children, a shift from a trial that centred on whether postpartum psychosis left her not criminally responsible; Assistant District Attorney Shanan Buckingham called the argument "laughable," and Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz said his office is still reviewing whether to retry. Judge William Sullivan ruled on nothing. (USA Today, WBUR)

items.title: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on 09-29 that Parliament will address AI safety in its fall sitting after media reports that OpenAI's ChatGPT coached the Tumbler Ridge shooter, without saying whether he meant the government's already-proposed digital safety bill or separate legislation.
items.html: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on 09-29 that Parliament will address AI safety in its fall sitting after media reports that OpenAI's ChatGPT coached the Tumbler Ridge shooter, without saying whether he meant the government's already-proposed digital safety bill or separate legislation. He said the government has been looking at social media and AI safety separately from British Columbia Attorney General Niki Sharma's request that Ottawa change the Criminal Code to make AI companies accountable. (Canadian Press via Medicine Hat News, The Toronto Star)

items.title: Australia's eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant said in Brisbane on Wednesday 09-30 (Tuesday evening in New York) that she may leave when her term ends in early 2027, and confirmed there is no plan to police AI chatbots through the under-16 social media ban.
items.html: Australia's eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant said in Brisbane on Wednesday 09-30 (Tuesday evening in New York) that she may leave when her term ends in early 2027, and confirmed there is no plan to police AI chatbots through the under-16 social media ban. She told reporters "10 years is a long time" and that the new digital duty of care makes it a good moment for new leadership; she said AI companies have shown they are not able or willing to regulate themselves, and that the existing framework could be strengthened further by the government. (Sydney Morning Herald)

items.title: Meta said on 09-29 it is expanding Instagram's School Partnership Program, now covering nearly 17,000 US schools, giving verified school partners Channels and Notes, and giving US high-school students who pass third-party verification a school banner, a Clubs & Teams directory, School Stories and Notes.
items.html: Meta said on 09-29 it is expanding Instagram's School Partnership Program, now covering nearly 17,000 US schools, giving verified school partners Channels and Notes, and giving US high-school students who pass third-party verification a school banner, a Clubs & Teams directory, School Stories and Notes. Meta says reports from school partners will be prioritised for review and points to its recent agreement with 52 bipartisan state attorneys general on teen restrictions. (Meta)

items.html: Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan registered, retrospectively, a completed 72-patient, non-randomized, single-blind study of a nurse-facilitated AI chatbot for psychological well-being and mental-health stigma among psychiatric patients in Amman, against usual care, with psychological well-being at two weeks, four weeks and three months as the primary outcome (first posted 09-29; the record lists a 2023-01-11 start and 2024-05-12 completion). items.title: Filament Health, the psilocybin developer owned by Ontario-based Rhelion Life Sciences, said on 09-29 that it has shipped its botanical psilocybin candidate PEX010 to the University of Calgary for PsiPTSD, a Phase 2 trial of psilocybin-assisted therapy for chronic PTSD in adult survivors of intimate partner violence (NCT06885996).
items.html: Filament Health, the psilocybin developer owned by Ontario-based Rhelion Life Sciences, said on 09-29 that it has shipped its botanical psilocybin candidate PEX010 to the University of Calgary for PsiPTSD, a Phase 2 trial of psilocybin-assisted therapy for chronic PTSD in adult survivors of intimate partner violence (NCT06885996). The university is the trial's sponsor, led by Dr. Chantel Debert, and Filament says it is only the drug supplier; it is Debert's second PEX010 trial, after a Phase 2b in persisting post-concussion symptoms. The release gives no start date or enrolment figure. (Rhelion Life Sciences via Newsfile)

items.html: Seattle Children's Hospital registered a 550-participant trial of a navigator program for rural youth involved in the legal system, combining flexible care management, family support, naloxone supplies and overdose education, against usual care (first posted 09-29; start planned 2026-10). Primary outcomes include overdose-prevention knowledge, any use in the past 30 days and days using alcohol and cannabis. (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07846735)

items.title: Korea University Ansan Hospital registered, retrospectively, a completed 31-patient non-randomized study of 10 weekly sessions of short-term dynamic psychotherapy added to medication in treatment-resistant depression, tracking Hamilton depression scores and prefrontal connectivity on functional near-infrared imaging against a healthy reference group (first posted 09-29; the record lists a 2022-02-15 start).
items.html: Korea University Ansan Hospital registered, retrospectively, a completed 31-patient non-randomized study of 10 weekly sessions of short-term dynamic psychotherapy added to medication in treatment-resistant depression, tracking Hamilton depression scores and prefrontal connectivity on functional near-infrared imaging against a healthy reference group (first posted 09-29; the record lists a 2022-02-15 start).
